policyDecision.scope: GitHub-hosted macOS and Windows feasibility evidence
policyDecision.skipSemantics: A skipped claim is outside the decision denominator. It is not a pass, failure, blocker, accepted deviation, or evidence of parity.

requiredDecisionChecks.description: The runner uses the reviewed Rust, Node, pnpm, and cargo-packager versions.
Cargo resolves the committed lockfile for the complete workspace.
The production graph contains one reviewed Zed revision and the controlled gpui-component vendor.
All Rust workspace tests pass from the committed lockfile.
The production-shaped GPUI package tests pass explicitly.
Frontend type checking and linting pass on the native runner.
License, SBOM, notice, asset, and installer-input policy checks pass.
The GPUI application links in release mode for the native target.
The release binary reports the bounded source and platform probe.
The release binary exercises the Vibex PTY and Alacritty model with raw bytes, CJK, resize, alternate screen, selection, and 10 MiB lossless throughput; Windows must use ConPTY.

The release binary loads the pinned native PDFium archive for the runner architecture and exercises CJK extraction, fit/zoom rendering, bounded page caching, and invalid-document handling without a window.
The native GPUI application initializes and remains alive for the bounded observation interval without making a pixel claim.
cargo-packager creates the reviewed native package with the registered application icon input.
The package installs into an isolated runner-owned location.
The installed package binary reports the same bounded source and platform probe.
Release binary, installed binary, package, config, and icon identities are recorded and consistent.
The isolated installation and its executable are removed.

requiredSkippedClaims.reason: GitHub-hosted runners are not used for reviewed real-window screenshots or native pixel comparison.
Hosted runner automation does not provide reviewed physical IME composition evidence.
Hosted runner automation does not provide reviewed real keyboard, pointer, clipboard, or drag-drop input evidence.
Hosted runner automation does not provide reviewed physical DPI or scale-transition evidence.
Hosted runner automation does not provide reviewed physical multi-monitor evidence.
